{"result":"# The Rust Programming Language and Memory Safety

Rust is a general-purpose language that emphasizes performance, type safety, concurrency, and memory safety [1]. Its central idea is memory safety without a garbage collector [2].

## Origins

Graydon Hoare started developing Rust in 2006 [2]. Mozilla Research later sponsored and maintained it from 2009, and the language was first publicly released in 2010 [2]. Version 1.0 followed in 2015 [2].

## What Memory Safety Means

Memory safety protects programs from bugs such as buffer overflows and dangling pointers [3]. Java achieves this through runtime checks of array bounds and pointer dereferences [3]. By contrast, C, C++, and Fortran allow arbitrary pointer arithmetic with no bounds checking, which makes them memory-unsafe [3].

## Rust's Approach

Rust's syntax is similar to C++, yet it guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector [2]. The language is also multi-paradigm, drawing on functional ideas such as immutability, algebraic data types, and pattern matching [1].

## Conclusion
